meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I want to know who decided on Owen's zero, and when.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Then who decided it, and on what?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. He writes in another file and pastes it in, so that shows a paste, not who wrote it. What else do you have?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine, he'll bring it. A paste at midnight isn't a zero. Go on.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote, Hale, and it could be from an edition or a study guide he used. Which edition is that, and did you check the others?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. Is anything on his file right now?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay, that's what outlines are for. And you didn't answer me: is anything on his file right now?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, private, before December 1, in writing tonight. Owen does it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. But I've asked you twice now, Hale: tell me nothing is on his file today.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth works. And tonight's email says in plain words what is on his file today, because you've ducked that three times.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Today you agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school on Thursday, November 12, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require written confirmation of exactly what is on Owen's file today, along with that agreement. I expect it in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She ended at her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday, November 12, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, all in writing tonight; she still wants written confirmation of what is on his file now. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: You put the made-up quotation beside the open play and let her search it herself, because it was a check on Owen's own essay she could make right there.
What cost ground: You never answered whether anything was on his file, even after she asked three times, and that is the one thing she never trades.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the work between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, which was very close to that kind of late night, and it is where her replies got shortest. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: The first time she asked whether anything was on his file, answer it plainly before you show the outline, so her one non-negotiable is settled early and stops coming back.
